validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION confirmed. Iraq's north-south 42-inch 'national dry gas pipeline' is real, operating, and correctly classed as a gas transmission trunk. (1) The sheet's own Jafar Dhia Jafar / Iraq Energy Institute presentation (iraqenergy.org, 2018 — GEM's RouteNotes source) has a slide 'Iraq's Existing Dry Gas Pipeline Connects North & South' and text 'interruption of 16-inch pipeline to the South (Taji)', confirming a physical N-S dry-gas backbone. (2) INDEPENDENT: Ahmed A. Al-Jibawi, 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq' (Iraqi Economists Network, June 2025) repeatedly names 'the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline' and describes multiple 2023-2025 branches bifurcating from it (Gharaf 20" for 76 km; a 42" spur at Mahmoodia south of Baghdad for 43 km to Basmaia PS; Khor Al-Zubair-Nadhum Shatt Al-Basrah 40 km 'to join the national dry gas pipeline'); it also cites OAPEC that Iraq's whole dry-gas network was 2,268.8 km end-2022 — a single ~600 km trunk fits inside that. (3) INDEPENDENT: Rudaw Arabic (2019) reports an operating 'أنبوب الغاز الوطني' (national gas pipeline) with a leak repaired at km 70 in Al-Muthanna Governorate, confirming the line is in service on its southern reach. Three independent origins agree it exists and operates. DIAMETER 42" is HIGH confidence (al-Jibawi states '42-inch national dry gas pipeline' explicitly and repeatedly; Jafar map corroborates the dry-gas backbone). Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is defensible (SCOP/North & South Gas Cos. under the Ministry; operator is really SCOP). FuelSource 'Saladin' fits the northern (Baiji/North Gas, Salah ad-Din) feed. NOT gem-only; NOT an oil/NGL line (the GulfPub Iraq oil list has no 42" N-S gas trunk match — the 42" oil 'Strategic Pipeline' Hadithah->Basra is a separate crude line, different corridor/origin).

validity.researcher_notes: SEGMENT / DOUBLE-COUNT RISK. P4061 is modeled as the whole N-S 42" national dry-gas trunk (600 km). P1852 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha Gas Pipeline' is ALSO 42", 470 km, ending at Nasiriyah (Dhi Qar) — geometrically this is almost certainly the Baghdad-area->Nasiriyah portion of the SAME mainline, i.e. a probable subset/relabel of P4061, not an independent pipe. The 'Trans-Iraqi-X' rows (P4062/P4064/P4065/P4066, all 24-18") read as city spurs branching off this trunk, and Al-Jibawi's paper + the Jafar map (which shows the Eastern Gas Pipeline 48"/350 = P4058, Taji-Duara = P4054, Al Mansuriya as pieces of one 'Existing Dry Gas Pipeline Connects North & South' system) support that these are all components of one national network. Cannot resolve the exact overlap from open sources; flagging so a human decides whether P4061 and P1852 (chiefly) represent one physical corridor entered twice. Confidence medium.

validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: 850 MMcf/d is not an independently stated throughput for this line. The only '850 mmscfd' in the Jafar PDF is 'Additional Associated Gas Processing Capacity Required for Other Oil Fields 850 mmscfd' — a national gas-PROCESSING shortfall figure, not this trunk's transport capacity. No independent source corroborates 850 MMcf/d for the pipeline; treat as low-confidence / likely mis-sourced. LENGTH: the sheet's Length [ref] (JCCP s2-3 seminar PDF) is DEAD (HTTP 404), and no open source states the trunk is exactly 600 km. OAPEC (via Al-Jibawi) gives the whole Iraqi dry-gas NETWORK as 2,268.8 km (2022), so 600 km for the mainline is plausible but unconfirmed. Not silently passing either number.

routes.corridor_desc: North-south dry-gas trunk following the Baghdad-Basra axis. Northern feed at the North Gas fields (Salah ad-Din / Baiji), running down through the Baghdad area (past Taji and Mahmoodia south of Baghdad), then along the mid-Euphrates/Diwaniyah-Samawah (Al-Muthanna, where the km-70 leak occurred) and Nasiriyah (Dhi Qar) corridor to the Basra/Khor Al-Zubair area in the south. Endpoints and several intermediate towns are sourced; the exact alignment (compressor stations, precise routing) is NOT published, so the corridor is a defensible band along the Baghdad-Basra highway/river axis, not a surveyed centerline. Loosely bounded — treat as a corridor, not a route.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the trunk's role ('Connects North & South' — North Gas/Salah ad-Din to Basra/South Gas) plus Al-Jibawi's branch descriptions that anchor waypoints (Mahmoodia bifurcation, Gharaf/Nasiriyah tie-in, Khor Al-Zubair join) and Rudaw's km-70 leak fixing the line into Al-Muthanna. All coordinates are real city/field locations (EPSG:4326), not invented; no compressor-station or centerline coordinates were fabricated. GEM's current start='Iraq'/end='Iraq' should become Salah ad-Din -> Basra with the waypoints above.

summary: P4061 National Gas Pipeline is REAL and operating (42" N-S dry-gas trunk, 3 independent sources, diameter HIGH); staged concerns: duplicate/segment overlap with P1852 (Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha 42"/470km) + Trans-Iraqi spurs, and spec (Capacity 850 MMcf/d mis-sourced, Length 600 km unverified w/ dead JCCP ref); route corridor Salah ad-Din(Baiji)->Basra staged at medium.
